newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Armenia to free Azeri PoWs before talks -Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Armenia to free Azeri PoWs before talks -Interfax.

text.p: Russia's Interfax news agency said on Tuesday that Armenia would free Azeri prisoners taken in fighting over the Nagorno-Karabakh enclave as a unilateral gesture of goodwill ahead of talks in Moscow later this week.
Officials in the Armenian capital Yerevan could not be contacted to comment on the report. It could not be independently confirmed.

Interfax, reporting from Yerevan, quoted an Armenian Foreign Ministry statement as saying: "By this move, Armenia confirms its devotion to agreements to free prisoners of war without preconditions on the principle of 'all for all'."

Saying Armenia believed in a compromise to end the conflict over Karabakh, it added that Armenian officials were working with the Red Cross to arrange the transfer of prisoners and urged Karabakh and Azeri leaders to follow suit.
It was not clear how many prisoners were involved.

Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan appointed the leader of the Karabakh separatists, Robert Kocharyan, as his prime minister last week in a move many analysts saw as hardening his stance on negotiations with Azerbaijan.
Azeri President Haydar Aliyev condemned the move on Tuesday.
He is expected to meet Ter-Petrosyan during a summit of former Soviet republics in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) to be held in Moscow on Friday.
Kocharyan on Tuesday denied his appointment meant a tougher stance but said he had no new ideas on how to solve the intractable conflict, which some fear could erupt again.

Nagorno-Karabakh, entirely within Moslem Azerbaijan's borders but populated mostly by Christian ethnic Armenians, broke away from Baku's rule in the late 1980s. Fighting killed thousands before a ceasefire was declared three years ago.
